bull.b: Updated ELPIS II analyses found fewer clinical and safety events and a statistically significant reduction in major adverse cardiac events. That evidence may support regulator discussions and preserve a development path in a high-risk pediatric indication, despite the primary endpoint miss.

The program has 52 issued patents, more than 60 pending, and five FDA expedited designations, including RMAT and Fast Track. This combination can protect the platform and support more efficient regulatory engagement as development advances.

An effective IND enables Laromestrocel to advance directly into a single Phase 2 registrational trial for pediatric dilated cardiomyopathy. This creates a defined next clinical step and broadens the lead candidate's potential beyond HLHS.

bear.b: ELPIS II failed its primary endpoint for improving right ventricular ejection fraction at 12 months. The result weakens the evidence for the HLHS program and may make regulatory advancement, trial interpretation, and further funding more difficult.

Cash of $10.1 million was expected to fund operations only into Q4 2026, while TTM operating and free cash flow were both about negative $20 million. Continued development therefore depends on financing or partnerships, creating material funding and execution pressure.

Quarterly revenue was only $0.3 million, down 10% year over year, while net loss widened 22% to $6.1 million as G&A and R&D increased. The weak revenue base and rising costs show limited operating leverage and no established commercial engine.
